title: Relative Motion: 1D Collinear & 2D Vector Frame Transformations

edges.title: 1D Motion Equations (v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at^2)
Resolution of 2D Vectors into Orthogonal Components

capabilities.statement: Calculate 1D relative displacement, relative velocity, and collision/overtaking times for two collinear bodies.
Interpret relative kinematic graphs: determine relative velocity from x_rel-t slope and relative displacement from v_rel-t Riemann area.
Formulate 2D relative velocity vectors using Cartesian components and calculate relative speed and orientation angle.
Solve canonical River-Swimmer problems: calculate minimum transit time and minimum drift crossing angles.
Solve canonical Rain-Umbrella problems: calculate apparent rain velocity vector relative to moving observer and umbrella hold angle.

representations.description: Closed vector subtraction triangle showing vec_v_A, vec_v_B, and the resultant relative vector vec_v_AB.
representations.pre_render_validation_gate: GATE-03 Vector resultant equality: vec_v_AB + vec_v_B == vec_v_A to 1e-4 tolerance.

representations.description: Relative displacement vs time x_rel(t) graph with intercept at initial separation and root at intersection time.
representations.pre_render_validation_gate: GATE-02 & GATE-06 Area integral validation: Riemann integral under v_rel(t) matches Delta_x_rel.

problem_families.archetype: Two parallel trains moving in same or opposite directions with constant velocities or constant accelerations.
problem_families.limiting_case: If speeds are equal in same direction, relative velocity is zero and separation remains invariant.

problem_families.archetype: Crossing flowing water of width d; finding condition for zero drift (v_swimmer >= v_river) versus minimum drift (v_swimmer < v_river).
problem_families.limiting_case: If river speed v_river = 0, transit time is simply d/v_swimmer and drift is zero.

problem_families.archetype: Vertically falling rain observed by running person; determination of tilt angle from vertical to avoid wetting.
problem_families.limiting_case: If person stops (v_man = 0), umbrella angle theta = 0 (held vertically upward).

misconceptions.statement: Assuming speed of approach is always the scalar sum |v_A| + |v_B| regardless of direction of motion.
misconceptions.refutation: Relative speed is magnitude of vector difference: |vec_v_A - vec_v_B|. For same-direction motion, speed of approach is |v_A - v_B|.
misconceptions.literature_ref: McDermott, L. C., et al. (1984). Student difficulties in kinematics.

misconceptions.statement: Believing that aiming directly across perpendicular to the riverbank takes the swimmer straight across with zero drift.
misconceptions.refutation: Water flow imparts downstream drift; to reach directly opposite bank, swimmer must aim upstream at sin(theta) = v_river / v_swimmer.
misconceptions.literature_ref: Halloun, I. A., & Hestenes, D. (1985). Common sense concepts about motion.

mandatory_falsifiers.assertion: Riemann area under v_rel(t) equals net relative displacement Delta x_rel.
